experiment_data.hypothesis: A capped or hybrid uniform+cate-error allocation can retain most group5 coverage/bias improvement from cate_error_product while reducing the overall CATE RMSE penalty relative to uncapped targeted allocation.

spec.command: bash -c "set -euo pipefail; cd /root/ec_hte; mkdir -p docs/results logs; /root/miniconda3/bin/python experiments/e006_capped_hybrid_allocation.py --n 5000 --reps 200 --budgets 100 500 1000 2000 --seed 20260531 --out docs/results/e006_capped_hybrid_allocation.json 2>&1 | tee logs/e006_capped_hybrid_allocation.log"
spec.checkpoint_source: e005_targeted_expert_allocation success-with-tradeoff result and D007 capped/hybrid allocation decision; no model checkpoint used
spec.eval_data: synthetic DGP generated by experiments/e006_capped_hybrid_allocation.py with n=5000, reps=200, budgets=[100,500,1000,2000], seed=20260531

hyperparams.cap_definition: single subgroup expert-label allocation share cap; capped_cate_error_25pct and capped_cate_error_35pct limit any one subgroup to at most 25% or 35% of total B
hyperparams.hybrid_definition: hybrid_50_50 and hybrid_70_30 mix uniform allocation weights with cate_error_product weights at 50/50 and 70/30 uniform/cate-error ratios

spec.notes: D007 follow-up to e005. e005 is interpreted as success-with-tradeoff because cate_error_product improved group5 coverage/bias but had small overall CATE RMSE cost; registry conclusion enum remains success.
